transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, the district will administer its required middle-school mathematics assessment on May 14, 2027, and I have final authority to approve the administration plan. I've asked each of you to review the draft before I give my approval. The draft currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. I'd like to go through each element of this plan and hear your feedback. Let's start with the testing coordinator -- any concerns about the proposed setup?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I have a significant concern with the room setup in the draft. My finalized roster does have 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. Because of that, I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students. However, I should note that this updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker, so we'll need to get that done before approval.

transcript.text: I need to raise a concern about the calculator portion of the draft plan. While reviewing the current state mathematics assessment manual this week, I found that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment, and they must be four-function calculators — not graphing calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, which would violate state guidelines. I have not yet amended the draft plan to reflect this, but it will need to be corrected before approval.

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I have a critical concern with the digital testing component of the draft plan. My device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and the district cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, and they confirmed that paper booklets are authorized as an alternative. However, this result has not yet been added to the plan, so the draft still calls for digital testing on school tablets, which will not work. We'll need to revise the plan to use paper booklets before approval.

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I have a concern with the storage component of the draft plan. My security review of the state testing agreement, which I completed this week, requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan currently calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, which does not meet these requirements. I have not yet updated the storage field in the draft plan, so it will need to be corrected before approval.
